title: `if-else` and `elif` Ladders 🪜
description: Add alternative paths with `else` and multiple conditions with `elif`.

slides.title: Two Roads: `else` 🛤️
slides.content:
## Choose Your Own Adventure

`if` runs code when a condition is true. What about when it's false? Use `else`.

```bash
if [ condition ]; then
   commands_if_true
else
   commands_if_false
fi
```
Exactly one of the two blocks will execute.

slides.title: Welcome Script with else
slides.codeSnippet:
read -p "Enter username: " user
if [ "$user" = "admin" ]; then
  echo "Welcome back, admin!"
else
  echo "Access denied."
fi

quizData.question: What does the `else` block do?

options.text: It runs when the `if` condition is true
It runs when the `if` condition is false

quizData.explanation: The `else` block only executes if the `if` condition evaluates to false.

slides.title: Multiple Choices: `elif` 🧩
slides.content:
## A Ladder of Tests

For more than two cases, chain with `elif` (else-if):

```bash
if [ condition1 ]; then
   ...
elif [ condition2 ]; then
   ...
elif [ condition3 ]; then
   ...
else
   default_action
fi
```
It checks conditions top to bottom and runs the first true block.

slides.title: Grade Classifier
slides.content: Translate a score into a letter grade:
slides.codeSnippet:
read -p "Score (0-100): " score
if [ $score -ge 90 ]; then
  grade="A"
elif [ $score -ge 80 ]; then
  grade="B"
elif [ $score -ge 70 ]; then
  grade="C"
elif [ $score -ge 60 ]; then
  grade="D"
else
  grade="F"
fi
echo "Your grade: $grade"

quizData.question: What keyword is used to add extra conditions between `if` and `else`?
quizData.explanation: `elif` (short for else-if) allows testing multiple conditions sequentially.

slides.title: Nesting `if` Inside `if` 🪆
slides.content:
## Deeper Decisions

You can place an entire `if` statement inside another:

```bash
if [ condition1 ]; then
   if [ condition2 ]; then
      echo "Both true"
   fi
fi
```
Use indentation to keep code readable.

slides.title: Nested Security Check
slides.codeSnippet:
if [ "$user" = "admin" ]; then
   if [ "$pass" = "secret" ]; then
     echo "Access granted"
   else
     echo "Wrong password"
   fi
else
   echo "Unknown user"
fi

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Too many nested `if`s? Consider using `case` or functions to keep your script tidy.
